g.text: An essential compendium of geography, economic performance, demography, and cultural landmarks.

text.tspan: Japan (Nippon/Nihon) is an East Asian island nation situated
along the Pacific Rim of Fire. Spanning an arc of 6,852 islands,
its four primary landmasses—Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, and
Shikoku—encompass over 98% of the country’s sovereign territory.
With rugged mountains covering nearly 73% of the land area,
its 124 million citizens primarily reside in dense urban coastal plains.

g.text: Administrative Divisions: 47 Prefectures grouped into 8 traditional geographic regions.

text.tspan: Japan stands as one of the world's most sophisticated post-industrial societies, balancing deep-seated ancient
traditions with vanguard technological leadership. Renowned for infrastructural mastery, safety, public transit efficiency,
and culinary artistry, the nation concurrently navigates structural head-winds including demographic aging and currency shifts.
